edges.description: Undigested trehalose reaching the colon draws water osmotically into the bowel lumen and is fermented by colonic bacteria capable of metabolizing trehalose, producing gas (hydrogen and/or methane) and loose, watery stools.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function TREH variants reduce or abolish alpha,alpha-trehalase activity at the small-intestinal brush border. Dietary trehalose, normally hydrolyzed to two glucose molecules for absorption, is not digested and passes largely intact into the colon.

evidence.snippet: Small-intestinal surgical biopsy specimens from 97 adult Greenlanders showed an incidence of trehalase deficiency in at least 8%.

evidence.reference_title: Low trehalase activity is associated with abdominal symptoms caused by edible mushrooms.
evidence.snippet: Trehalase activity was determined in serum and on a duodenal biopsy specimen obtained by endoscopy.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of genetic variation that determines human trehalase activity and its association with type 2 diabetes.
evidence.snippet: Four tag SNPs in TREH were genotyped in these subjects and plasma trehalase activity was highly associated with three SNPs: rs2276064, rs117619140 and rs558907 (p = 2.2 × 10(-11)-1.4 × 10(-23))

nodes.description: Unhydrolyzed trehalose passing into the colon causes osmotic water flow into the bowel lumen; colonic bacterial fermentation of the unabsorbed sugar (when gas-producing microflora are present) adds hydrogen/methane gas production, bloating, and flatus to the osmotic diarrhea.
